description:
Kesen-cha is a local green tea of the old Kesen district on the Pacific coast of Iwate: Ofunato, Rikuzentakata and Sumita. Iwate is well to the north of most Japanese tea country, which makes it a curiosity even before you taste it.

How it is grown and made is little recorded. What applies is the general pattern of Japanese green tea, so treat any specific claim with care.

The same goes for taste. Brew it as an ordinary sencha-type green tea and see what the lot gives you.

If you find it, it will most likely be a small local product. Ask who grew it and when; that is more useful than the regional name.
history: Little is documented. The tea is recorded as a named product of Ofunato, Rikuzentakata and Sumita in Iwate, but its beginnings and development are not well recorded in accessible accounts.
